title: Most seven-day deep-earthquake pair excess occurred in the first day under a 20-degree shuffle in 2000-2025
abstract: We split a published seven-day pair excess by lag. We used 785 ComCat earthquakes deeper than 300 km with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 in 2000-2025. We counted same-year pairs within 200 km Earth chord distance. We shuffled times within each year and 20-degree cell in 9,999 draws. The first day had 110 pairs against a null mean of 71.10. Days 1-7 had 65 against 59.12, with an upper-tail p-value of 0.1945. The first day supplied 86.9% of the descriptive seven-day count excess. Days 7-30 also gave no clear excess in the primary grid. A shifted 20-degree grid gave a days 1-7 p-value of 0.0140. Thus later evidence depends on grid boundaries. The result narrows the time scope of a prior result on the same data. It does not show that later clustering is absent, count caused aftershocks, or identify a physical recovery time. Sparse events, mixed magnitude types, catalog errors, and the shuffle assumptions limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, all null draws, a scalar audit, and external-data retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: Lag counts under the primary year and 20-degree cell shuffle. Red lines show observed counts. Histograms show 9,999 null draws. The count range is a null reference, not a confidence interval for a physical effect.

citations.reason: We split its seven-day pair count by lag and use the same shared snapshot and primary shuffle. This is overlapping evidence, not independent confirmation.
Its selected large-center test found late excess under a different null. Our all-event pair shuffle asks a different question.
